subject: Pilot engine recommendations — post-demo recap, benchmarks & next steps
messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.f@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.j@finlytics.com>, Carla Mendes <carla@finlytics.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.c@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.c@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 21 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Pilot engine recommendations — post-demo recap, benchmarks & next steps

Thanks again for a great demo earlier this week — appreciate the detailed product context and the sample query set you shared. Per our conversation, I pulled together a concise engine slate we recommend for a 4–6 week pilot along with operational tradeoffs and the artifacts you asked for (prompt set + benchmark PDF attached below). Quick summary up front and proposed next steps at the bottom.

Recommended pilot slate (three engines, prioritized):
1) Redwood-2-3B-PTQ (primary) — rationale: best cost/latency mix for your interactive search UX; very low token cost when using PTQ on A100-ish GPUs. Estimated median p95 latency (512-token context): ~120ms; expected per-1M-token cost: ~$18 (hosted commit pricing estimate). Quality: high for short answers and entity extraction; slightly lower on long-form synthesis.
2) Mistral-7B-v1 (fallback / accuracy check) — rationale: strong instruction-following and factuality on your internal corpus; higher token cost than Redwood-2-3B but noticeably better on multi-step reasoning prompts. Median p95 latency: ~200ms; per-1M-token cost: ~$28.
3) Llama-2-13B-Quant (long-tail / recall-heavy queries) — rationale: best quality on long-context synthesis and multi-document summarization; run as on-demand tier or cached offline for batch jobs due to higher latency/cost. Median p95 latency: ~420ms; per-1M-token cost: ~$62.

Benchmarks and artifacts attached: pilot benchmark PDF includes throughput curves, p95 latency by sequence length, and prompt-specific regression scores vs your sample set. Also included: finlytics-demo-prompt-set-v1.json (canonical prompts we used) and pilot-mock-queries.csv. Links at the bottom.

Operational notes:
- Batching profile: for your traffic shape (short bursts, many concurrent users) we suggest conservative batching (max batch size 8) to keep p95 latency under 200ms while recouping cost on low-util periods.
- Caching: enable prefix cache for your frequent query templates (we saw ~22% token reduction on repeated prefixes in the sample set).
- Regression guardrails: we recommend an eval guardrail on ROUGE/QA F1 on a 150-sample regression set (we flagged a few hallucination patterns during the demo).

Open questions for you (so we can size pilot):
- Will you be able to share a 500–1,000-row de-identified sample of live queries (CSV)? That will let us run a tighter latency/cost projection.
- Any hard SLA expectations for p95 latency?
- Procurement / PO cadence — do we need a formal SOW to kick off the Reserved Pilot?

Next steps (proposed):
- I: Redwood runs a 5-day inference benchmark on the sample (we’ll use the attached prompt pack) — ETA 3 business days after sample arrives. (Owner: Naomi)
- II: Ben will flesh out the pilot pricing sheet (hosted + burst reserved fallback) and share a draft. (Owner: Ben)
- III: Alex/Carla to confirm pilot success criteria (quality thresholds + target cost per 1M tokens). (Owner: FinLytics)

Thanks — I’ll wait to get the sample CSV and procurement contact.

—
Naomi Feldman
Sales Engineering
Redwood Inference

Attachments: finlytics-demo-prompt-set-v1.json (prompt pack), pilot-mock-queries.csv (sample queries), benchmarks-20270521.pdf (latency & regression summary)

Thanks Naomi — slate looks sensible. Two quick asks: 
1) Add a short regression-run checklist in the benchmark PDF (we should call out anchor prompts + expected F1 thresholds so procurement can see objective gates).
2) Add an explicit fallback policy mapping in the pilot pricing sheet: primary => Redwood-2-3B-PTQ, degrade to Mistral-7B when latency spikes > 750ms, and Llama-2-13B for nightly batch jobs only.

I’ll take the pricing draft and put in the reserved vs burst columns.

–Ben

Alex — great questions. Quick answers and I attached the CSV export and a worked 4-week estimate in the attached PDF. See highlights below and I put the files in the Drive folder as well.

1) Raw benchmarks: attached \"benchmarks-20270521.pdf\" includes the CSV export link and per-prompt latency table (Drive link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aB-customer-demo-pack). If you prefer the raw CSV, I included it as an attachment.

2) 4-week cost worked example (assumptions in the sheet):
- Usage: 1k DAU * 3 req/day * 28 days = 84k requests
- Mean tokens/request = 180 => total tokens = 15.12M tokens
- Estimated token mix: 70% Redwood-2-3B-PTQ (primary), 25% Mistral-7B (fallback), 5% Llama-2-13B (batch/edge cases)
- Resulting cost (hosted pilot estimate): Redwood-2-3B @ $18/1M => 10.584M tokens = $190.51; Mistral-7B @ $28/1M => 3.78M tokens = $105.84; Llama-2-13B @ $62/1M => 0.756M tokens = $46.87. Total ~= $343 for 4 weeks (token-only estimate; we'll include margin for throughput/infra and request routing in the formal pilot pricing).

3) Regression set: 200 labeled QA pairs is a good starting point — we recommend adding 50 anchor prompts that have historically tripped hallucinations (we flagged three patterns during the demo). With that set we can run automatic quality gates and surface failure modes within the first benchmark run.

Next small asks from our side: please share the procurement contact/email so we can route the PO/SOW draft. Also confirm whether your infra team wants the raw CSV or the PDF summary in their ticket.

If helpful, I can block a 20-min sync Monday to walk procurement through the worked example and the fallback rules.

—
Naomi

Attachments placed in Drive and included inline: benchmarks-20270521.csv (raw), benchmarks-20270521.pdf (worked example + CSV), finlytics-demo-prompt-set-v1.json
